extracted.intended_audience: International doctoral candidates applying for DAAD bi‑national/cotutelle doctoral scholarships (research stays in Germany)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for applying to the DAAD Bi‑nationally Supervised Doctoral Degrees / Cotutelle scholarship, including eligibility, required documents, funding details, and the selection criteria used by the independent selection committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme options (sandwich vs cotutelle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two possible options: Option a) Doctorate with bi‑national supervision ('sandwich model') where the doctorate is started at home university, includes research stays in Germany, completed at home university and awarded by home university; Option b) Doctorate following the 'Cotutelle' procedure where the doctoral project is carried out at both universities under an individual cooperation agreement and the degree is awarded jointly by both universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the option that matches your situation; for option b a Cotutelle contract (cooperation agreement) is required (or submitted later before funding begins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — academic degrees and doctoral status
rubrics_metrics.description: Option a: You can apply if you have earned a Master’s degree or Diplom (or in exceptional cases a Bachelor’s degree) at the latest at the start of the funding period. Option b: You can apply if you have been admitted to a doctoral programme at the latest at the start of the funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure degree/admission status is valid by the funding start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — recency of graduation / start of doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, applicants should not have graduated any longer than six years before the application deadline. If you have already started your doctorate, the start of the doctorate should not be longer than 3 years ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Important Scholarship Information / Section A, point 2 for exceptions or further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency exclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application cannot be considered, if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate past residence carefully; rule is firm for application consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, other regulations are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to www.daad.de/extrainfo for field‑specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: What can be funded — research stays in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: Option a: research stays at a state or state‑recognised institution of higher education or a non‑university research institute in Germany (as part of a doctoral programme in the home country) are funded. Option b: research stays at a state or state‑recognised institution of higher education in Germany to complete a bi‑nationally supervised thesis are funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research visits must be to recognised institutions; plan and justify choice of host institution in the proposal and study plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is provided for between 7 and a maximum of 24 months. Grants can initially be awarded for a maximum of 24 months. You can apply for an extension for a possible fourth year of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selection committee determines length based on project and study plan; academic progress is assessed annually to determine continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible allocation of grant time
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant can be used flexibly for several shorter stays during your doctoral project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying, outline in your study plan and time schedule how you intend to divide your time between Germany and your home university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for visits to other countries
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to visit other countries (e.g. to collect material), specify these plans in your application. Such visits can only be funded if they take place in connection with your visit to Germany and they do not exceed one quarter of your expected total funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit non‑Germany travel to <= 25% of total funded time and demonstrate connection to German visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding start year requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding must begin in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project schedule accordingly; no funding start outside stated year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary value — monthly stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly payments for doctoral candidates during the stay in Germany: 1,400 euros. No scholarship payments are made during stays at your home university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for periods at home university without stipend; plan visits to Germany when stipend applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional monetary components
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover; travel allowances for up to three outward and return journeys unless covered by the home country or another source; a research allowance of €460; travel and accommodation expenses for supervising university teachers for one trip of up to 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate supervisor trips in the time schedule when applying; benefits from third parties are partially credited toward the DAAD scholarship (see Important Scholarship Information Section F, point 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional benefits for long uninterrupted stays and family
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances, for uninterrupted stays of over 6 months in Germany you can apply for a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Important Scholarship Information (section F, points 3 and 9) for conditions and documentation required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability / chronic illness subsidy
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a disability or chronic illness: on application, a subsidy may be provided for justified additional costs incurred abroad necessary to realise the project in Germany and not covered by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each case is reviewed individually (see important information for scholarship applicants, section F, point 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language training support
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD offers payment of course fees for an online language course after receipt of the Scholarship Award Letter; possibly funds a language course (2, 4 or 6 months) before the start of the research stay; allowance for a personally chosen German language course during the funding period; reimbursement of the fee for a TestDaF or DSH test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAAD decides whether to fund pre‑stay courses and for how long depending on language skills and project. If a language course is granted and the host institute's working language is German, participation is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and independent committee
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent selection committee consisting of specialist scientists reviews applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on funding period and continuation are the committee's responsibility; academic achievements assessed annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic achievements (grade point average, development of grades); Academic progress; Knowledge of the language(s) of instruction or working language(s); If applicable, scholarly achievements after graduation (e.g. publications, lectures, conference papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transcripts, evidence of progress, and any post‑graduation scholarly output to strengthen this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Quality of research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of research proposal and preparation (originality, topicality and relevance of the project, choice of host institution and first contacts); Feasibility and consistency of study plan and time schedule; Incorporation of project within the overall doctorate (in terms of content and time), if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a well‑prepared research proposal (max. 10 pages) discussed with the German academic adviser and a realistic schedule; explicitly explain host selection and integration into your doctorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Potential of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Career prospects: significance of the research project and stay in Germany for further academic, professional and personal development; Motivation: academic and personal reasons for wanting to visit Germany, German language skills (if different from working language); Non‑study‑related activities: non‑study‑related knowledge and skills, civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter of motivation (1–2 pages) should address 'What do you hope to gain from your project in Germany (personally, professionally, for your career)?' and demonstrate motivation and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection committee also gives due consideration to equal opportunities; applicants can provide relevant information in the application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, supply information that the committee should consider under equal opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Curriculum vitae
rubrics_metrics.description: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tabular CV format and adhere to 3‑page maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — List of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: List of your published publications (max. 10 pages), if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include up to 10 pages; only include relevant scholarly output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Letter of motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of motivation (1–2 pages): describe your academic and personal reasons for your planned project in Germany and answer what you hope to gain from your project in Germany (personally, professionally, for your career).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under ‘study project/motivation’ in the DAAD portal; be specific about gains and motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal (max. 10 pages in total): description of your research project prepared and formulated by yourself and discussed with the academic adviser in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under ‘research project’ in the DAAD portal and consult Important Scholarship Information / section B, point 2 for formatting/content guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Schedule / study plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule (informal) for planned research work for the entire funding period (including possible extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline division of time between Germany and home university and indicate trips (e.g. supervisor visits) in the time schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Declaration on safety/ethics from German supervisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration from the scientific supervisor in Germany on safety‑relevant and ethical aspects of the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload this document in addition to the confirmation from the academic host under ‘Scientific ethics/research safety‘.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Proof of admission/enrolment and degree certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of admission to/enrolment for doctoral studies at the home university, if applicable; University degree certificate (e.g. Bachelor, Master) indicating final grade(s). If not yet available at application, it must be submitted before the scholarship begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include translations (German or English) if original is in another language; DAAD may later request certified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Supervisor confirmations (Option a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option a) Bi‑national supervision: Written confirmation, agreed and signed by both academic advisers. The confirmation must refer to your project and guarantee that the host institute in Germany will provide you with a workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research project must have been agreed with both academic advisers; upload under ‘acceptance of host institution’.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Cotutelle contract or interim confirmation (Option b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Option b) 'Cotutelle model': Individual cooperation contract between the home university and the cooperating German university (Cotutelle contract). If not yet available at application, submit it later before the funding period begins; in that case upload a confirmation from your academic adviser in Germany referring to your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under ‘acceptance of host institution’; cotutelle contract must be finalised before funding begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document — Letter of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: One recent, supporting letter of recommendation from a university teacher which provides information about your qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate the recommendation form in the DAAD Portal during the application period, send it to the referee, and upload the completed form under 'Letter of Recommendation'. Follow portal instructions closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Other documents which support your application (examples: certificates of employment, proof of practical training/internships or voluntary commitment, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only relevant supporting documentation to strengthen your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format, translation and certification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates, proof of credits, certifications and translations may be scanned in non‑certified form and uploaded. If you submit documents in your national language, include German or English translations. The DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload PDFs only; keep originals and be prepared to provide certified copies if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/application portal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Application via DAAD portal only: register in portal, complete online application, upload attachments as PDF. The portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET or CEST) on the last application day. Access to the application portal only appears while the current application period is running.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not wait until final day to submit; if documents are to be sent by post, use postmark date as dispatch proof. Contact portal@daad.de or the technical hotline for portal problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application is only valid if you submit all the required documents to the DAAD portal by the application deadline. Incomplete applications cannot be considered. You are responsible for ensuring that your applications are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double‑check that all required uploads are present before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: File type restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: You can only upload PDF files to the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scan paper documents and save in PDF format; include translations together with the original document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing window
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for this scholarship programme are possible in the period June until the stated application deadline. Application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter and in most cases are in the same period as the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current dates on the DAAD site and plan registration/submission within the open portal window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor travel expenses policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel and accommodation expenses according to the German Federal Travel Expenses Law for your supervising university teachers for one trip of up to 10 days—to Germany to monitor progress, and to your home university to take part in final examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the planned supervisor trips in the time schedule when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party benefits crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits from third parties are partially credited towards the DAAD scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Important Scholarship Information (section F, point 6) for rules on crediting third‑party support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and support for portal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have technical questions or problems your local information and advice centres cannot help you with, contact portal@daad.de or the technical portal hotline on weekdays from 9–12 and 14–16 (CET/CEST) on +49 (0) 228 882‑8888.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for processing times when seeking technical help; plan ahead for portal submissions.
